plan.title: feat(scope): operator-authorized correction of a clause's required axis after activation that keeps its test evidence

narratives.Description: After activation, the only sanctioned fix for a criterion whose words set a wrong strict axis is the operator's not_applicable grant, which replaces the criterion's test evidence with a false record. This story adds a second mode of the same operator grant, `--clear-axis`, that drops only the named axes for one item, keeps its test evidence and is bound to the item text and declaration fields. The scope:complete gate reads the correction only from the operator's grant store, never from the brief, so CI applies none. The #6591 declaration-hides-axis row turns from warn to enforce, so a declaration added to an already active brief cannot clear an axis without the operator.
narratives.Overview:
1. Grant mode. `deft authz:grant -- --template acceptance-disposition --plan-ref <scopeId> --story-ids <itemId> --clear-axis <axis>[,<axis>] --reason <text> --confirm`. The mode has its own surface-prefix constant. `--clear-axis` is refused with `--disposition` or `--deferred-to`; a stored grant that carries both prefixes is malformed; `viewOf` returns null for a correction grant, so the disposition path and older runtimes ignore it. Mint path, main-clone store, 24-hour default expiry, single use, replay and revoke are unchanged.
2. Mint checks. The mint refuses an item without an id and an axis that the item's text does not infer. Before the typed confirm it prints each covered item's fenced text, every match of each named axis with no cap (its own uncapped list from the same matcher the #7099 explainer uses; the explainer's three-match cap stays for advisories), and the evidence pointer it will keep.
3. Binding. The grant records the existing cover digest and one digest of the text `inferTextStrictAxes` reads plus the eight declaration fields. Any change refuses at `scope:complete` and prints the re-grant command.
4. Resolution. A separate resolver keys corrections by item and axis, supersedes only within that key, refuses when a live correction and a live disposition cover the same item, and never adds to `grantedClauses`. `scope:complete`, the `complete-cohort` dry run and restamp use it.
5. Gate input. `evaluateAcceptanceEvidenceGate` takes an optional correction map from its caller and never reads a correction from the item. A caller without the store (CI closeout) passes none. For a corrected item the remaining axes use today's rule; when the correction removes the last strict axis, only `kind: test` with a valid test pointer passes. A correction never counts as a `merge` declaration.
6. Record. The completed write adds `x-directive/axisCorrection` (`axes`, `reason`, provenance with `grantId`, `recorded_at`) and keeps `x-directive/evidence`; the mid-flight active write does not carry it. Restamp rewrites it from the store grant or refuses. The completed-write guard checks its shape and requires `grantId`. The key joins `ITEM_MACHINE_KEYS` in `scope-provenance/known-machine.ts`, with a `KNOWN_MACHINE_WRITERS` entry naming `packages/core/src/scope/transition.ts`; no existing brief carries it, so no intent digest changes. Machine class is safe because the record is audit only: no gate reads it as authority.
7. Declarations after activation. The `declaration-hides-axis` row (#6591), in `warn` since 0.130.0, turns to `enforce` under the table's own rule: `verify:scope-provenance` exits 1 when a declaration changed after activation newly hides a strict axis, against the merge-base copy it already reads. The row text names the fix: remove the declaration; for a test-proven criterion the operator records `--clear-axis` at completion. Stated limit (operator, comment 7089490270): a declaration added in the change that activates the brief (merge-base copy outside `xbrief/active/`) is reviewed with the activation, and the refusal is at merge, not at the local `scope:complete`.
8. Refusal. For a `kind: test` mismatch on an item with an id, the `scope:complete` refusal prints the `--clear-axis` command for that item and its text axes as the path for a test-proven criterion, and the `not_applicable` command (#7099) for a criterion that does not apply. An id-less item is reported as not targetable. The `xbrief:preflight` advisory names the same command. A printed reason is fenced.
9. Stated limits in `content/docs/scope-provenance.md` and `content/commands.md`: the activating-change limit of item 7; the hand-written disposition gap (#3240); the store trust; used-grant replay on a matching digest; `scope:stamp-evidence` still skips strict-axis items, so test evidence is recorded as today.
10. One PR, built after #7099 merges (that PR moves `formatAcceptanceDispositionCommand` into `acceptance-evidence.ts` and rewrites the same refusal tail): `acceptance-evidence.ts`, `acceptance-disposition-grant.ts`, `runtime/src/authz.ts`, `transition.ts`, `complete-cohort.ts`, `lifecycle/completed-write-guard.ts`, `refusal-declarations/table.ts`, `scope-provenance/evaluate.ts`, `declaration-hides-axis.ts` and `known-machine.ts`, their tests (`remedy-runs.test.ts` and the closeout tests included), the two docs above, one `changelog.d/` fragment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Given an active story whose `clause.1` text infers `deploy` and has `kind: test` evidence, when the operator mints `--clear-axis deploy` for `clause.1` and `scope:complete` runs, then the gate passes, the clause is still walked, and the completed item keeps its test evidence plus an `x-directive/axisCorrection` record citing the grant id.
- [ ] Given the same story with no correction, when a change adds `x-directive/requires: merge` to that item while the merge-base copy of the brief is under `xbrief/active/`, then `verify:scope-provenance` exits 1 with the `declaration-hides-axis` row naming the correction, and `scope:complete` without the declaration still refuses the `kind: test` evidence; when the merge-base copy is under `xbrief/pending/` (the activating change), no row fires, as the stated limit says.
- [ ] Given a brief with an intent pin whose item gains `x-directive/axisCorrection` in the change that moves it from `active/` to `completed/`, then `verify:scope-provenance` reports no intent drift and no unclassified key for that field.
- [ ] Given an `x-directive/axisCorrection` written by hand on an active item, then `evaluateAcceptanceEvidenceGate` ignores it, in `verify:pr-closeout-attestable` and in `scope:complete`.
- [ ] Given a correction for `deploy` on an item whose text infers `smoke` and `deploy`, then `kind: smoke` passes and `kind: test` is refused; given a correction that removes the only axis, then `kind: test` passes and `kind: review` and `kind: merge` are refused; other items keep their axes.
- [ ] Given a correction, when the item's title, id, narrative fields, clause text or declaration fields change, then `scope:complete` refuses the correction and prints the re-grant command.
- [ ] Given a live correction and a live `not_applicable` grant for the same item, then `scope:complete` refuses; given two corrections for different axes of one item, both apply; a correction grant never deletes evidence or joins `grantedClauses`.
- [ ] Given a correction-mode mint on an item with five `deploy` matches, then before the confirm it prints the item's fenced text, all five matches including the last, and the kept evidence pointer; it refuses an axis the text does not infer and an item without an id.
- [ ] Given a completed brief whose `x-directive/axisCorrection` cites a grant that is not in the store, when `scope:complete` restamps it, then it refuses and names a re-grant; a completed write whose record has no `grantId` is refused by the completed-write guard.
- [ ] Given an active story that fails `scope:complete` on an axis mismatch with `kind: test` evidence, then the refusal prints the `--clear-axis` command for that item and its axes and the `not_applicable` command, and for an id-less item says that no grant can target it; the `xbrief:preflight` advisory names the same command.

- Trusting an on-disk correction record in the gate or in CI (Stop 1 D4; comments 7087663778 finding 1, 7087664062 finding 1, 7087664337 finding 1).
- Taking the activated copy from the newest commit that added the path, or from any git history read at `scope:complete` (Stop 1 D5; comments 7087663778 finding 2, 7087664062 finding 2, 7087664337 finding 4). The merge-base copy at `verify:scope-provenance` is the base.
- Admitting `kind: review` once a correction leaves no axis (comment 7087664062 finding 3, comment 7087664337 finding 2). Comment 7087663778's answer to question 4 preferred today's rule; the lean takes the narrower rule because `x-directive/evidence` is machine-writable after the mint.
- A separate template, or a `test` declaration token, as this authority (all three answers to question 2). A pre-activation `test` token narrower than `merge` is a separate issue (comment 7087664062 finding 11).
- Bringing hand-written dispositions into this PR (comment 7087664062 finding 8; comment 7087664337 answer 3).
narratives.UserStory: As a Directive operator, I want to correct the required axis of one criterion after activation while keeping its test evidence, so that a test-proven criterion can complete with a true record and an agent alone cannot clear the axis.

## In plain English
`scope:complete` decides from the words of a criterion whether it needs deploy, smoke, UAT or observed-behaviour evidence. Sometimes the words are wrong: a criterion about how code handles deployment records needs no deployment, and a unit test proves it. Before activation the author can declare the real requirement on the item. After activation the only sanctioned fix is the operator's `acceptance-disposition` grant with `not_applicable`, which deletes the test evidence and records the criterion as "not applicable". That record is false: the criterion applies and was tested. The #7099 arc split this out.

2. **Prefer the same template with an explicit, mutually exclusive mode.** Reuse minting, storage, revocation and replay handling. Separate the mode in parsing and resolution, not merely in a surface-prefix constant. A `test` declaration is attractive because it states the intended requirement directly, but it still needs authenticated post-activation authorization, revision binding and CI validation. It does not remove the difficult part.

3. **Some completion-time protection is necessary for AC2; D5 is not sufficient as specified.** The existing warning deliberately does not enforce. 4. **Do not require only `kind: test` for every corrected item.** Clearing a false deploy axis from an item that still requires smoke must continue to admit smoke evidence. When no strict axis remains, accepting review evidence follows the existing suitability rule. State that consequence explicitly; if the operator is authorizing test-only acceptance, that is a different grant contract.

5. **A separate correction record alongside unchanged evidence is appropriate.** It preserves both the result and the operator’s decision. A shape-only record is not proof of that decision. CI needs independently trusted authorization or must refuse to honor the correction.

**Evidence:** At the dispatch pin, `pr-closeout-attestable/evaluate.ts` calls `evaluateAcceptanceEvidenceGate(brief.plan)` without grant-store validation. ## Summary

Split from the #7099 design-critique arc by operator decision (leftover of pain P1; recommendation comment 7087240963).

`scope:complete` infers a strict axis from words in a clause, so a test-proven clause about deployment data needs deploy evidence. Before activation an author can declare the clause's real requirement. After activation the only sanctioned path is the operator `acceptance-disposition` grant, which marks the whole criterion `not_applicable` and replaces its test evidence. This issue asks for an operator-authorized correction of a clause's required axis after activation that keeps its test evidence (for example an axis-only grant, or a `test` declaration token with a post-activation authorization rule).

Refs #7099

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Given an active story whose clause has a text-inferred strict axis and recorded `kind: test` evidence, when an operator records the correction for that clause, then `scope:complete` accepts the test evidence and the completed record keeps the test pointer instead of a `not_applicable` disposition.
- [ ] Given the same story with no operator correction, when an agent edits the active brief alone (for example adds a declaration), then the axis is still required and the #6591 warning still fires.
- [ ] Given a correction for one axis on one item, then other axes and other items keep their requirements, and `kind: merge` evidence stays unsuitable unless merge is declared.
- [ ] Given a correction, when the clause text it was recorded for changes, then `scope:complete` refuses the correction and names a re-grant.
- [ ] Given an active story that fails `scope:complete` on an axis mismatch with `kind: test` evidence, then the refusal names this correction as the path for a test-proven clause.

sentences: Grant mode. `deft authz:grant -- --template acceptance-disposition --plan-ref <scopeId> --story-ids <itemId> --clear-axis <axis>[,<axis>] --reason <text> --confirm`. The mode has its own surface-prefix constant. `--clear-axis` is refused with `--disposition` or `--deferred-to`; a stored grant that carries both prefixes is malformed; `viewOf` returns null for a correction grant, so the disposition path and older runtimes ignore it. Mint path, main-clone store, 24-hour default expiry, single use, replay and revoke are unchanged.

Mint checks. The mint refuses an item without an id and an axis that the item's text does not infer. Before the typed confirm it prints each covered item's fenced text, every match of each named axis with no cap (its own uncapped list from the same matcher the #7099 explainer uses; the explainer's three-match cap stays for advisories), and the evidence pointer it will keep.

Binding. The grant records the existing cover digest and one digest of the text `inferTextStrictAxes` reads plus the eight declaration fields. Any change refuses at `scope:complete` and prints the re-grant command.

Resolution. A separate resolver keys corrections by item and axis, supersedes only within that key, refuses when a live correction and a live disposition cover the same item, and never adds to `grantedClauses`. `scope:complete`, the `complete-cohort` dry run and restamp use it.

Gate input. `evaluateAcceptanceEvidenceGate` takes an optional correction map from its caller and never reads a correction from the item. A caller without the store (CI closeout) passes none. For a corrected item the remaining axes use today's rule; when the correction removes the last strict axis, only `kind: test` with a valid test pointer passes. A correction never counts as a `merge` declaration.

Record. The completed write adds `x-directive/axisCorrection` (`axes`, `reason`, provenance with `grantId`, `recorded_at`) and keeps `x-directive/evidence`; the mid-flight active write does not carry it. Restamp rewrites it from the store grant or refuses. The completed-write guard checks its shape and requires `grantId`. The `declaration-hides-axis` row (#6591), in `warn` since 0.130.0, turns to `enforce` under the table's own rule: `verify:scope-provenance` exits 1 when a declaration changed after activation newly hides a strict axis, against the merge-base copy it already reads. Refusal. For a `kind: test` mismatch on an item with an id, the `scope:complete` refusal prints the `--clear-axis` command for that item and its text axes as the path for a test-proven criterion, and the `not_applicable` command (#7099) for a criterion that does not apply. An id-less item is reported as not targetable. The `xbrief:preflight` advisory names the same command. A printed reason is fenced.

Given an active story whose `clause.1` text infers `deploy` and has `kind: test` evidence, when the operator mints `--clear-axis deploy` for `clause.1` and `scope:complete` runs, then the gate passes, the clause is still walked, and the completed item keeps its test evidence plus an `x-directive/axisCorrection` record citing the grant id.

Given the same story with no correction, when a change adds `x-directive/requires: merge` to that item while the merge-base copy of the brief is under `xbrief/active/`, then `verify:scope-provenance` exits 1 with the `declaration-hides-axis` row naming the correction, and `scope:complete` without the declaration still refuses the `kind: test` evidence; when the merge-base copy is under `xbrief/pending/` (the activating change), no row fires, as the stated limit says.

Given a brief with an intent pin whose item gains `x-directive/axisCorrection` in the change that moves it from `active/` to `completed/`, then `verify:scope-provenance` reports no intent drift and no unclassified key for that field.
Given an `x-directive/axisCorrection` written by hand on an active item, then `evaluateAcceptanceEvidenceGate` ignores it, in `verify:pr-closeout-attestable` and in `scope:complete`.

Given a correction for `deploy` on an item whose text infers `smoke` and `deploy`, then `kind: smoke` passes and `kind: test` is refused; given a correction that removes the only axis, then `kind: test` passes and `kind: review` and `kind: merge` are refused; other items keep their axes.
Given a correction, when the item's title, id, narrative fields, clause text or declaration fields change, then `scope:complete` refuses the correction and prints the re-grant command.

Given a live correction and a live `not_applicable` grant for the same item, then `scope:complete` refuses; given two corrections for different axes of one item, both apply; a correction grant never deletes evidence or joins `grantedClauses`.

Given a correction-mode mint on an item with five `deploy` matches, then before the confirm it prints the item's fenced text, all five matches including the last, and the kept evidence pointer; it refuses an axis the text does not infer and an item without an id.

clauses.text: Grant mode. `deft authz:grant -- --template acceptance-disposition --plan-ref <scopeId> --story-ids <itemId> --clear-axis <axis>[,<axis>] --reason <text> --confirm`. The mode has its own surface-prefix constant. `--clear-axis` is refused with `--disposition` or `--deferred-to`; a stored grant that carries both prefixes is malformed; `viewOf` returns null for a correction grant, so the disposition path and older runtimes ignore it. Mint path, main-clone store, 24-hour default expiry, single use, replay and revoke are unchanged.

Mint checks. The mint refuses an item without an id and an axis that the item's text does not infer. Before the typed confirm it prints each covered item's fenced text, every match of each named axis with no cap (its own uncapped list from the same matcher the #7099 explainer uses; the explainer's three-match cap stays for advisories), and the evidence pointer it will keep.

Binding. The grant records the existing cover digest and one digest of the text `inferTextStrictAxes` reads plus the eight declaration fields. Any change refuses at `scope:complete` and prints the re-grant command.

Resolution. A separate resolver keys corrections by item and axis, supersedes only within that key, refuses when a live correction and a live disposition cover the same item, and never adds to `grantedClauses`. `scope:complete`, the `complete-cohort` dry run and restamp use it.

Gate input. `evaluateAcceptanceEvidenceGate` takes an optional correction map from its caller and never reads a correction from the item. A caller without the store (CI closeout) passes none. For a corrected item the remaining axes use today's rule; when the correction removes the last strict axis, only `kind: test` with a valid test pointer passes. A correction never counts as a `merge` declaration.

Record. The completed write adds `x-directive/axisCorrection` (`axes`, `reason`, provenance with `grantId`, `recorded_at`) and keeps `x-directive/evidence`; the mid-flight active write does not carry it. Restamp rewrites it from the store grant or refuses. The completed-write guard checks its shape and requires `grantId`.
